title: Council committee and board appointments for 2025–2026
subtitle: Dog designation committee concerns, term-limit exemptions, added closed-session item and a late-night special meeting
overview: A special Council meeting on December 16 filled council seats on standing committees, boards and advisory bodies for the 2025–2026 term, along with citizen appointments. Most current council appointments were carried over. Changes were made to the Wilfrid Laurier University Board of Governors, the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee and the Multicultural Centre of K-W board.

Council approved the list of citizen appointments {{vote:m3}}, amended to change one name on the Committee of Adjustment. Three long-serving citizen members were exempted from the term limit in the appointments policy so they could be reappointed. One recommended Heritage Kitchener nominee withdrew and was removed from the list.

Before the appointments, Council added a closed-session item about an identifiable individual and met in closed session on legal advice, a third-party matter and that item. The minutes report no decisions from it. Council also heard that the Dog and Animal Designation Appeal Committee may need professional expertise, and staff will explore options. This matters to residents because these appointees shape local advisory work and appeal rights.

decisions.detail: Council approved the recommended advisory and quasi-judicial committee appointments, as amended, and the Centre in the Square board candidate {{vote:m3}}.
An amendment replaced one recommended Committee of Adjustment member with another candidate before the appointments were approved.

decisions.item: Waive notice for added closed-session item
decisions.detail: Council waived notice, with two-thirds support, to add an urgent closed-session item about an identifiable individual.
Council authorized a closed session after the meeting on a solicitor-client privilege matter, a third-party confidential matter and the added personal matter.

debate: Staff said the missing council appointments on the draft list, such as the Kitchener in Bloom Committee, were clerical omissions and would be corrected.

One councillor asked to step off the Grand River Accessibility Advisory Committee because of a work-schedule conflict. Another councillor was nominated and accepted, then asked to withdraw. A third councillor was then put forward.
The Mayor explained that Wilfrid Laurier University's board has a six-year term limit, so the Mayor must step aside for at least a year and a councillor was nominated in their place.

Councillors said the Dog and Animal Designation Appeal Committee would benefit from a professional dog behaviour expert. The Mayor cautioned that making it a quasi-judicial body would remove the appeal to Council and leave only judicial review. Staff said hearings were hard to schedule without enough members.
